findings.title: Negation and target scope leak across independent actions
findings.description: The splitter omits English full stops and analyse processes only the first deletion verb. Negation is any earlier negative token, even when it negates retaining/necessity rather than deleting. Thus ordinary affirmative conclusion-deletion advice gets no 149-word warning; reversing the sentences can instead produce a spurious ambiguity. Semicolon and single-positive controls pass. The advice survives normalization and copying unchanged but lacks its required length warning.

limits: Targeted common advice syntax, not exhaustive natural-language analysis.
All scenarios use production normalize_evaluation and evaluation_text; no browser rendering.
Expected deletion is specified from the literal advice, never inferred from product helper output.
